A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. v1 ends at the references despite referring to appendices; v4 supplies Appendices A-I. No unresolved reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection and fairness experiments, backbone comparisons, robustness tests, visualizations, and ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds empirical results in the appendices, including DFDC-trained models, FairFD comparisons, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Structural Fairness Decoupling, Global Distribution Alignment, channel selection, and the training losses remain unchanged in Section 3. Appendix D adds pseudocode documenting the training workflow; it does not establish a changed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds DFDC as a training source within the four previously evaluated datasets. Appendix I adds FairFD evaluation, but neither PDF explains FairFD's data composition or overlap with those datasets. The extent of genuinely new dataset or population coverage, beyond changed training and evaluation protocols, therefore remains uncertain.

E2.justification: Appendix I substantially expands evaluated comparators with RECCE, UCF, Capsule, FFD, CORE, F3Net, SPSL, SRM, and BPFA-processed variants. Tables I.3-I.6 add these methods to comparisons on the original datasets. DAG, DAW, and PFGDFD match the existing DAG-FDD, DAW-FDD, and PG-FDD comparisons rather than constituting additional methods.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces DFDC-source training with Xception and ResNet-50 and evaluation across the four retained datasets. Appendix I adds FairFD protocols reporting naive, approach-averaged, and utility-regularized fairness metrics beyond the original metric set. The original experiments' stated optimizer, batch size, epoch budget, and loss weight remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds loss-weight sensitivity and fairness-accuracy tradeoff analyses in Appendix G and demographic feature t-SNE comparisons in Appendix H. Appendices B-C also supply the DFD/DFDC corruption results and ResNet-50 decoupling analysis that v1 references without including. These substantially expand the available robustness and mechanism evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new FairFD STD entries are presented as fairness metrics, not uncertainty estimates across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 4 revises several values: DFDC GDA+SFD AUC changes from 58.46 to 61.86 and Celeb-DF AUC from 74.75 to 76.75, matching the already reported values in Table 2. Numerous appendix results are newly supplied, including DFDC-trained models and expanded comparisons. On FairFD, the method reports DPD 0.0159 versus SPSL's 0.0203, but AUC 0.7026 versus FFD's 0.7304. These are new comparisons, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning in Equations 1-10 are retained. v4 adds no theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or revised formal assumption; the additional benchmark metrics are tabulated without new mathematical definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims: combining structural decoupling with distribution alignment improves demographic fairness while maintaining detection performance and generalization. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly acknowledges dependence on accurate demographic annotations and the restriction to gender and race. Appendix G explicitly discusses the fairness-accuracy tradeoff, while Appendix H interprets demographic feature mixing as evidence of common forensic fingerprints. These add substantive qualifications and mechanism interpretations absent from v1.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents sample counts and demographic categories, including 76,139 FF++ training samples, 25,386 validation samples, and 25,401 test samples. Algorithm 1 documents nested decoupling/training loops and subgroup sampling. These materially expand reproducibility information without establishing changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: v4 adds Liu et al.'s 'Thinking Racial Bias in Fair Forgery Detection: Models, Datasets and Evaluations' to support the FairFD comparison. The original related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged; most citation-number changes reflect this single added reference.

P1.justification: The main prose and section order remain essentially intact. v4 adds appendix sectioning, resolves the original Appendix ?? references to A-C, and adds a CVPR 2026 acceptance footnote. There is no extensive rewriting or reorganization of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds appendix tables, robustness and sensitivity plots, demographic t-SNE panels, and an algorithm box. Tables I.3-I.6 redisplay retained results with methods arranged as columns alongside new comparators. The original main figures and table structures are largely preserved; Table 4's numerical corrections are separate result changes.

improvement.justification: v4 improves completeness and reproducibility by supplying previously missing appendix material, documenting samples and training loops, and reconciling Table 4 with the main results. Broader comparisons and explicit limitations also help assess the method. However, new reporting problems limit the gain: Table E.2 gives Fairadapter gender es-AUC 68.17 above overall AUC 60.78, contrary to Equation 10, and Appendix I's broad superiority statement overlooks FFD's higher FairFD AUC. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
